english.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial verb for pondering or having a thought in mind.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for thinking about something, including whether to do it.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for thinking carefully about something or reflecting on it.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for thinking carefully about something.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for thinking carefully about something.
This is the all-purpose spoken choice for trying to work out or puzzling over a difficult matter.
Use this for thinking something over rather than physically chewing it.

examples.english: I think about whether to go see a movie tomorrow.
examples.traditional: 我諗緊聽日去唔去睇戲。

examples.english: I consider whether to go tomorrow.

examples.english: I took time to meditate on it before deciding whether to buy it.

examples.english: I’ll ponder it first; I don’t want to answer you so quickly.

boxes.meaning: to think, reckon (as in 我諗)

english.note: Use this, especially as 我諗, for “I guess” meaning “I think” or “I reckon” without stressing uncertainty.

examples.english: I guess it will rain tomorrow.
examples.jyutping: ngo5 nam2 ting1 jat6 wui5 lok6 jyu5
